feeds.title: Kids' Book Review
feeds.description: Kids Book Review is a voluntary children's literature and book review which works with authors, illustrators and publishers Australia-wide and internationally. We cover news, reviews, interviews, articles, guest posts, events, specialist literacy articles and much more, attracting readers from all over the world including teachers, librarians, industry professionals and parents and kids.

feeds.title: The Childrens Book Review
feeds.description: The Children's Book Review, named one of the ALSC (Association for Library Service to Children) Great Web Sites for Kids, is a resource devoted to children's literature and literacy. We publish reviews and book lists of the best books for kids of all ages. We also produce author and illustrator interviews and share literacy based articles that help parents, grandparents, caregivers & teachers.

feeds.title: Mr. Schu Reads
feeds.description: I am a part-time lecturer at Rutgers University and the Ambassador of School Libraries for Scholastic. I work diligently to put the right book in every child's hand. Book trailers are one way to connect readers with books. (All opinions shared are on own.)

feeds.title: Writing for Kids (While Raising Them)
feeds.description: Street magic performer. Hog-calling champion. Award-winning ice sculptor. These are all things Tara Lazar has never been. Instead, she writes quirky, humorous picture books featuring magical places that everyone will want to visit.

feeds.title: Free Kids Books Blog
feeds.description: Free Kids Books is a growing library of unique children's books and resources. Follow to get updates.

feeds.title: BookBound Blog
feeds.description: Sam J.D. Thomas is a book blogger who reviews children's and middle-grade books. He has a passion for reading and believes that books can be a powerful tool for learning and growth. In his blog, he shares his thoughts on the latest books, as well as older classics. Sam is a great resource for anyone who loves children's books. He is always up-to-date on the latest releases and has a knack for finding hidden gems.

feeds.title: The Strawberry Post » Children's Book
feeds.description: The Strawberry Post is a magazine-style blog that aims to entertain, educate, and inspire readers. It covers a wide range of topics, including lifestyle, travel, food, and entertainment. Read articles and reviews on Children's book in the following section.

feeds.title: James Preller's Blog
feeds.description: James Preller is a children's book author. In his blog, he shares his experiences, thoughts, and insights on writing and publishing children's books. He also includes book reviews, resources, and creative inspiration. Preller's blog is a great resource for anyone interested in writing or publishing children's books. He provides valuable insights into the writing process, the publishing industry, and the marketing of children's books.

feeds.title: Lydia Lukidis
feeds.description: Lydia Lukidis is the author of 50+ trade and educational books for children. Her passion for reading and writing began at a very young age, when she was a voracious reader and composed poem after poem in her journals. She's especially fond of writing books with stimulating STEM topics, while keeping the text accessible and engaging for young readers. She also continues writing fiction and poetry.

feeds.title: Violet Lemay
feeds.description: Violet Lemay is a children's book illustrator and author. The blog provides insights into Violet Lemay's publishing journey, her creative projects, and her involvement in promoting and celebrating children's art.

feeds.title: A Kids Co. Blog
feeds.description: Explore big ideas, tough questions, and challenging topics for kids. Grownups, it's hard to know what to say to every question your kid has. These stories, facts, podcasts, and books help you navigate all the things your kids wonder about from racism, love, death, empathy, and so much more.

feeds.title: Lindsey McDivitt Blog
feeds.description: Lindsey McDivitt writes fiction and non-fiction for children including picture book biographies A Plan for the People: Nelson Mandela's Hope for his Nation and Nature's Friend: The Gwen Frostic Story. Her first fictional picture book, Christmas Fairies for Ouma, was published in 2022.

feeds.title: Kidliomag
feeds.description: Kidliomag is a kid's literary digital Magazine designed to spark your child's interest in reading and writing. This is a literary resource for parents and teachers. They support all kinds of books and self-published authors through our marketing programs and services.

feeds.title: Tinted Edges » Childrens Books
feeds.description: Angharad writes this is a blog for the books she reads and collects. When it comes to books, she is a sucker for a pretty face. Angharad is also an avid reader and loves to think about books long after she has finished them. She uses this blog for all the reviews and to feature great books and editions she comes across.

feeds.title: The Chrysalis BREW Project » Children's Book
feeds.description: Welcome to The Chrysalis BREW Project, an Australia-based award-winning platform catering to all content creators and readers worldwide! This is where you'd find thoughts, words, photos, videos, and other ideas in the realm of Books, Reviews, and Everything Written (BREW).

feeds.title: World Kid Lit
feeds.description: World Kid Lit is an online resource that promotes and celebrates children's and young adult literature from around the world. They offer a wealth of information and resources that can help you discover new books, learn about different cultures, and connect with other people who share your passion for children's literature.

feeds.title: Provo Library Children's Book Blog
feeds.description: The Provo Library Children's Book Blog is a great resource for parents and teachers looking for new and exciting books for children. The blog features reviews of new releases, as well as classic favorites. There are also posts on a variety of topics related to children's books, such as reading tips, author interviews, and book lists.

feeds.title: The Chronicles Of A Children's Book Writer - Earl Dizon
feeds.description: In 'The Chronicles of a Children's Book Writer' blog, the author, Earl Dizon, shares his reading experiences and reviews of various books. He provides ratings and brief comments on each book, sharing his thoughts and recommendations.

feeds.title: NBPB Reviews Blog
feeds.description: Dive into inquisitive, fun reviews of Children's Picture books that are educational, impactful, and enlightening. NBPB Reviews Blog is managed by a group of book lovers passionate about discovering and sharing the world of picture books. The goal is to provide insightful, informative, and entertaining reviews of some of today's best picture books.

feeds.title: Lisa Connors
feeds.description: Lisa's debut picture book, Oliver's Otter Phase ( Arbordale Publishing, 2018) is fiction with a lot of science woven in. It's fun reading, but also useful in the classroom to begin a unit on adaptations. This website has information about picture books Lisa encounters that really speak to her with links to lesson plans she's written that can be used with some of the books.

feeds.title: Judy Bradbury Blog
feeds.description: Judy Bradbury is a children's book author, literacy specialist, and writing teacher. She writes books that inspire conversations, open minds, and expand possibilities. Her website provides information about Judy, her children's books, professional services, and a blog. Judy offers professional services such as school visits, writing workshops, professional development and parent programs, creating educators' guides for children's books by other authors, and editorial services for aspiring writers.

feeds.title: The Children's Bookroom
feeds.description: Deborah Furchtgott has a Ph.D. from Harvard in medieval poetry and is currently doing freelance developmental editing and copyediting. She is passionate about children's literature, so this is a space for her to discuss the books she loves.

feeds.title: Maria Marshall Blog
feeds.description: Maria Marshall, fueled by a passion for storytelling from an early age, channelled her creativity into writing and crafting imaginative adventures for her siblings. Committed to fostering a love of reading, Maria advocates for the power of board books, picture books, and chapter books to ignite imaginations. Through interviews with authors and illustrators, as well as reviews spanning from board books to middle grades, she celebrates the magic of children's literature and makes nature exploration enjoyable for all through books and photography.

feeds.title: Celebrate Nonfiction
feeds.description: Celebrate Nonfiction is a blog that celebrates the wonders of science through the lens of nonfiction books. The blog is written by a teacher who believes in the power of nonfiction to inspire and inform young readers. She regularly posts about award-winning nonfiction picture books, as well as other nonfiction books that she thinks are worth sharing. The blog is a great resource for teachers, parents, and anyone who wants to learn more about the amazing world of science.

feeds.title: Sonderbooks » Children's Fiction Review
feeds.description: Sondra Eklund is a librarian and book lover who also loves math, knitting, and theology. Sondra has been writing reviews on this website since 2001 and blogging since 2006. Read Children's Fiction Review by Sandor on the following page on the blog.

feeds.title: Books Around The Table
feeds.description: Books Around The Table is the blog of Margaret Chodos-Irvine, Laura Kvasnosky, Julie Larios, Julie Paschkis, and Bonny Becker. They are a critique group of children's book authors and illustrators who have been meeting monthly since 1994 to talk about books they are working on, books they have read, their art, and their lives.

feeds.title: Books Up North » Kids Review
feeds.description: Books Up North is run by Sarah Tyson, a literary consultant and events producer who has been described as a 'book ambassador' creating bridges so that readers and writers can meet. She has a passion for books and a strong belief in the power of reading to change lives. Books Up North is a literary event consultancy serving the North of England. They have a mission to promote literacy in its broadest context by organizing book festivals, author events, and workshops.

feeds.title: Cotsen Children's Library
feeds.description: The Cotsen Children's Library at Princeton University is a specialized library dedicated to children's literature. Their website provides information about the library, its collections, events, and blog posts written by the curatorial staff.

feeds.title: Children's Book Council
feeds.description: The Children's Book Council (CBC) is the nonprofit trade association of children's book publishers in North America, dedicated to supporting the industry and promoting children's books and reading. Dedicated to supporting the children's publishing industry through programming that connects and educates publishing professionals, advocates for a more inclusive industry, and shines a light on the books, creators, and resources available for young readers.

feeds.title: Anita Loughrey's Blog
feeds.description: Anita Loughrey's blog is her journal about her experiences and thoughts on writing. As well as news about me and her books, it includes writing tips, book reviews, author interviews, and blog tours.

feeds.title: Mom Read It
feeds.description: Rosemary, the vibrant mind behind Mom Read It, thrives as a children's and YA librarian within a bustling public library system. With a zest for storytelling, maker spaces, and coding, she champions advocacy initiatives. An avid comic book aficionado, she juggles the roles of bibliomaniac, knitter, and mother to her beloved 'dragons' (aka boys). Her blog brims with enthusiasm for kids' literature, YA gems, and occasional forays into adult reads, reflecting her diverse passions and unwavering dedication to fostering a love of reading in young minds.

feeds.title: Good Reads with Ronna
feeds.description: Ronna Mandel, a freelance writer for esteemed publications like JLife and L.A. Parent magazines, wears many hats, including that of a dedicated mother. Her passion for writing extends to all things reading-related, along with parenting, education, and special needs topics. With a discerning eye, Ronna delves into the latest literary releases, offering insightful reviews and recommendations for books and reading-related products tailored to kids and families alike.

feeds.title: The Baby Bookworm
feeds.description: The Baby Bookworm is the home of JJ, a 7-year-old bibliophile who reads a new book every single day. The blog started as a way to keep track of the books they read but ended up finding lots of friends who want to know what books are right for their little ones. So JJ and Mama started The Baby Bookworm, a review blog across multiple platforms, to share literary adventures with other young book lovers.

feeds.title: Bank Street College of Education » Center For Children's Literature
feeds.description: For more than a century, Bank Street College has led the charge to place students' needs at the center of practice and policy in the field of education. Since its beginnings in 1916, Bank Street has been at the forefront of understanding how children learn and grow. The Young Reviewers Committee chooses a book and one of the young reviewers writes a summary of the book. The blog also includes other information about the Center for Children's Literature, such as upcoming events and awards.

feeds.title: Jestress's Forgotten Books and Stories
feeds.description: Jestress's Forgotten Books and Stories is a website dedicated to discussing and reminiscing about old children's books. The creator, Tracy Christenson, is a book hoarder with a particular interest in children's literature. The site aims to help people remember and find half-remembered books from their childhood.

feeds.title: Daniel Boone Regional Library
feeds.description: The Daniel Boone Regional Library strives to be at the heart of the community, a trusted resource and partner known for excellence, creativity, and open, equitable access, connecting every person to opportunities for a lifetime of discovery, learning, and joy.

feeds.title: School Library Journal
feeds.description: School Library Journal is a monthly magazine that provides reviews of books, media, and other resources for children and young adults. It is published by School Library Media Group. The magazine was founded in 1914 and is the oldest journal in the field of school librarianship. It is a valuable resource for librarians, educators, and parents who want to find high-quality resources for children and young adults.

feeds.title: Swimming in Books Blog
feeds.description: Rebecca is a writer and school librarian in South-West London. At the moment she works in an Academy Trust which includes a primary and a secondary school so I get to read all the the age groups! Swimming in Books is a great resource for parents, teachers, and librarians who are looking for new books to recommend to children.

feeds.title: Nashville Public Library » Children
feeds.description: The Nashville Public Library's homepage provides access to various online library services, including catalog browsing, educational resources, and event information. Users can find books, movies, music, and other materials available for borrowing or streaming. The website also offers databases, special collections, and research assistance.

feeds.title: Lauri Fortino's Frog On A (B)Log
feeds.description: Welcome! Frog On A (B)Log is the site of children's picture book author, freelance writer and transcriptionist, and retired library assistant Lauri Fortino, and her frog friend Finley. You will find oodles of picture book related content on the pages of this blog. If you like to read, write, share, or celebrate picture books, then you will like this blog!

feeds.title: Momma Braga » Childrens Books
feeds.description: Melanie Braga is the owner and writer of Momma Braga. She graduated from Humber College with a Social Service Worker diploma. This platform was established to document her journey in life and in parenthood. She hopes that through her blog, she can inspire and help others. This is why she prides herself on sharing the journey of other parents as she feels we can all learn from one another and support each other. Read children's book reviews in the following section.

feeds.title: The Crimson Review of Children's & YA Literature
feeds.description: The Crimson Review blog is a compilation of children's and young adult book reviews composed by graduate students enrolled in the Children's and Young Adult Materials and Services courses at The University of Alabama's School of Library and Information Studies.

feeds.title: Jill's Book Blog » Children
feeds.description: Jill is a writer in Toronto, Ontario. She reviews six books a week. Jill has studied English, publishing, and creative writing. She also has a Masters in Creative and Critical Writing from the University of Gloucestershire. She is currently querying agents with her contemporary young adult novel about a Princess in England.

feeds.title: Children's Literature Assembly Blog
feeds.description: The Children's Literature Assembly (CLA) of the National Council of Teachers of English is a professional community of children's literature enthusiasts who advocate the centrality of literature in children's academic and personal lives.

feeds.title: The Kaz Windness Blog
feeds.description: Kaz Windness loves to make her readers laugh. Kaz is an award-winning, genre-crossing illustrator and author of heart-warming books for young readers. Proudly neurodiverse (Autstic-ADHD), Kaz specializes in character-driven books celebrating inclusivity, grit, and kindness.

feeds.title: Helping Kids Rise Blog
feeds.description: Helping Kids Rise is a non-profit organization that highlights and increases access to diverse and inclusive children's books. They believe that every child should have access to books that educate, empower, and inspire. Diverse children's book recommendations; including picture books, middle-grade books, early chapter books, and more!

feeds.title: Book Riot - The Podcast
feeds.description: News in the world of books and reading, including hot industry releases, adaptations, publishing industry events, and more with Book Riot's Jeff O'Neal and Rebecca Shinsky.Book Riot is the largest independent editorial book site in North America and home to a host of media, from podcasts to newsletters to original content, all designed around diverse readers and across all genres.

feeds.title: Cooperative Children's Book Center » Book of the Week
feeds.description: The CCBC is a unique and vital gathering place for books, ideas, and expertise in the field of children's and young adult literature. The CCBC is a noncirculating examination, study, and research library for Wisconsin school and public librarians, teachers, early childhood care providers, university students, and others interested in children's and young adult literature.

feeds.title: Hey, Look! A Writer Fellow!
feeds.description: A groovy little website by children's book author Mike Allegra. The website features information about Mike Allegra, his writing samples, books, and blogs. Read articles on various categories, including book news, essays/book reviews, and family and/or autobiography.

feeds.title: STOOMIO
feeds.description: Eddy is the creator of this marvelous place. His aim for Stoomio is to bring all book lovers together and he will be doing his bit to bring you the latest and greatest in what children's authors and illustrators have been creating for all to enjoy.

feeds.title: Literary Potpourri » Childrens Books
feeds.description: Mallika shares her love for reading and mentions her favorite authors, including Enid Blyton, Bobbsey Twins, Nancy Drew, Conan Doyle, Agatha Christie, and many others. Mallika enjoys reading a variety of genres, including detective fiction, history, historical fiction, children's books, young adult fiction, popular science, maths, fantasy, classics, and humor. Read reviews on Children's book in the following segment.

feeds.title: Miriam Laundry Blog
feeds.description: The blog by Miriam Laundry Publishing Corporation is dedicated to children's books and covers various topics related to writing, editing, illustrations, book design, publishing, marketing, motivation, and lifestyle. The blog offers valuable resources and free training, including a Children's Book Masterclass, Picture Book Editing Package, and Children's Book Blueprint.

feeds.title: Zetta Elliott Blog
feeds.description: Zetta Elliott is a black feminist writer of poetry, plays, essays, novels, and stories for children. Elliott is an award-winning author, educator, and playwright who has written over 30 books for children, teens, and adults. She is also the founder of the non-profit organization Rosetta Press, which publishes books by underrepresented authors.

feeds.title: Middle Grade Ninja
feeds.description: Rob Kent interviews fellow authors, editors, literary agents, and other publishing professionals to discuss the craft and business of producing middle grade and young adult novels. New episode every Saturday.MiddleGradeNinja.com.

feeds.title: ALSC Blog
feeds.description: Coverage of time sensitive news in children's librarianship, current issues in the field, and programs, conferences, initiatives, resources, and activities. The Association for Library Service to Children (ALSC) is a network of more than 4,000 children's and youth librarians, children's literature experts, publishers, education and library school faculty members, and other adults committed to improving and ensuring the future of the nation through exemplary library service to children, their families, and others who work with children.

feeds.title: Storytime Magazine
feeds.description: Storytime is the UK's favourite illustrated monthly story magazine for kids aged 3 to 8. It's filled with classic fairy tales, myths and legends, folk tales, fables, poems and rhymes, stories from around the world and tales from today. Read the Storytime Blog for top tips and advice on boosting your child's literacy, reading for pleasure, and news and insights on the world of stories.

feeds.title: From the Mixed-Up Files…
feeds.description: A group blog of middle-grade authors celebrating books for middle-grade readers. For anyone with a passion for children's literature. Join us!

feeds.title: KidLit411
feeds.description: Your one stop information shop for children's writers and illustrators. Our goal is to organize relevant information about writing and illustrating for children in one handy spot, right here.

feeds.title: Children's Books Daily Blog
feeds.description: Children's Books Daily is a guide for parents and a resource for educators, curated by Megan Daley.Its the author's own little space on the interwebs where she connects with other parents, educators, readers and creators of books about all things children's and YA literature. This is a space where you'll find information and tips, guidance, reviews and more.

feeds.title: Becky's Book Reviews
feeds.description: Becky from Becky's Book Reviews, Young Readers, and and Operation Actually Read Bible. I love reading. Always have, always will. The views and opinions expressed on this blog are mine and mine alone.

feeds.title: A Kids Book A Day
feeds.description: My name is Janet Dawson, and I am the K-8 librarian at six schools (two middle and four elementary) in the HampdenWilbraham Regional School District, Massachusetts. Every day, I post a review of a book published in 2017. I choose books that I have personally enjoyed, that I feel would be useful in an elementary classroom, and most of all, that I think children would like.

feeds.title: Imagination Soup Blog
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Melissa Taylor, mom, writer, & former elementary teacher & literacy trainer. This is a place where parents, librarians, and teachers can find good children's books as well as engaging learning ideas, resources, and community. My ultimate goal is to make your life easier and for kids to find the right books to hook them on reading.

feeds.title: Kids Book Explorer
feeds.description: Here you'll find announcements, reviews and surveys in relation to children's book industry events: book launches, illustration exhibitions, authors talks, this blog's partnerships and collaborations, etc.

feeds.title: Gecko Press Blog
feeds.description: Gecko Press is an independent publisher of curiously good award-winning children's books based in Wellington, New Zealand.

feeds.title: Here Wee Read
feeds.description: Diversity & Inclusion Expert, Charnaie Gordon helps you find quality diverse & inclusive books for kids and kid-friendly educational products. She is dedicated to shaping our family culture around books. Here Wee Read is a blog resource dedicated to connecting people with diverse, and inclusive books.

feeds.title: Let's Talk Picture Books
feeds.description: A blog that features children's picture book and comic book reviews, illustrator interviews, and global picture book exchanges, all from a design and illustration perspective. Authored by Mel Schuit, a picture book enthusiast with an MA in Children's Literature.

feeds.title: Blazer Tales Blog
feeds.description: Book Talks, Book Reviews, Book Trailers, First Chapter Friday and so much more. Authored by Laurie Evans, a book-loving librarian with a passion for getting the right book into the hand of a child so that they will develop a love of reading!

feeds.title: Nerdy Book Club Blog
feeds.description: If you love books, especially those written for children and young adults, then you are an honorary member of The Nerdy Book Club. Nerdy Book Club was designed to give us a home to share that love of reading with others as well as to organize voting and announcing winners of our First Annual Nerdies Book Awards.

feeds.title: Literacious
feeds.description: A place to explore children's literature offering families, librarians, and teachers booklists, resources, and reviews to engage the readers in their lives. Authored by Laura Arnhold.

feeds.title: Only Picture Books
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Ryan. My goal is to create and compile PB-related information that will be of value to writers, illustrators, teachers, librarians, agents, editors, publishers, and publicists who enjoy PBs are much as I do. In many ways, OPB is both a celebration of the picture book community and a curated resource, as well.

feeds.title: Nosy Crow Blog
feeds.description: Nosy Crow is an award-winning independent children's book and app publisher. We began publishing child-focused, parent-friendly children's books and apps in January 2011 with the aim of creating books and apps that encourage children to read for pleasure.

feeds.title: Bobs Books Blog
feeds.description: Children's and Young Adult Book Reviews by Bob Docherty. Discover interviews with inspiring people, hints and tips from renowned photographers, travelers and other experts. Stories from around the world written by us

feeds.title: Birdhouse Books
feeds.description: Trish Rucker is a southern girl who blogs about books, ephemera, life, love, dogs, and all things vintage, particularly vintage children's books. Birdhouse Books is an online shop that sells unique vintage goodies like vintage children's books and holiday cards.

feeds.title: Jilanne Hoffmann's Blog
feeds.description: Jilanne Hoffmann is a children's book author, a freelance writer for nonprofit organizations, and currently enjoys writing stories for kids. Through this blog, she writes picture books reviews.

feeds.title: Kids Books NZ Blog
feeds.description: Kids Book NZ Blog reviews books because they are passionate about promoting New Zealand children's books. They promote children's books written by New Zealand authors. They will do their best to cover as many titles as possible even if this takes them a while. They appreciate your understanding in this matter. Go through their blog to learn more about their work.

feeds.title: Society of Children's Book Writers & Illustrators Blog
feeds.description: Learn the essentials of publishing children's books, improve your craft, and stay current with industry practices. The Official Blog of the society of children's book writers and illustrators. Authored by Lee Wind. The Society of Children's Book Writers & Illustrators supports quality children's books and the artists who make them.

feeds.title: Did You Ever Stop To Think Blog
feeds.description: Reviewing and talking about children's literature, graphic novels & bookish things. Shiny.

feeds.title: Pratham Books Blog
feeds.description: Uplifting stories about the world of books, reading, and children. Pratham Books is a leading nonprofit bringing storybooks to children across India in their mother tongue languages.

feeds.title: Ms. Yingling Reads Blog
feeds.description: Ms. Yingling Reads is a middle grade book blog covering genres like adventure, fantasy, history, humour and more. The blog's focus is on realistic, middle grade fiction, middle grade nonfiction, young adult fiction suitable for ages 11-14, and some pictures reviews.

feeds.title: Charlotte's Library
feeds.description: At Charlotte's Library, readers delve into a world of science fiction and fantasy literature for kids and teens, sprinkled with diverse genres. Charlotte, an archaeologist by day and volunteer for a small New England library by night, immerses herself in the realms of fantasy and science fiction. With a passion for storytelling, she invites visitors on a literary journey filled with adventure and wonder.

feeds.title: Kristi's Book Nook
feeds.description: Kristi's Book Nook provides parents with children's book reviews along with author interviews and book giveaways.

feeds.title: Bookworm for Kids
feeds.description: Reviews for children books from toddlers to teens and everything in between.

feeds.title: Library Lady Blog
feeds.description: News and reviews from the world of children's books. Anne Thompson, a retired school librarian, also produces a weekly round up of news highlights and links to online reading for pleasure resources for librarians, teachers and parents.

feeds.title: Jabber Works
feeds.description: Illustrator and writer Sarah McIntyre is easy to spot in her pointy glasses and hats. Sometimes she writes and draws picture books and comics herself, sometimes she illustrates books for other people, including Giles Andreae, Alan MacDonald, Gillian Rogerson, Anne Cottringer and Claire Freedman.

feeds.title: Kid's Picture Book Review
feeds.description: Looking for a Children's Book Influencer? Kid's Picture Book Review can help you get found and get you reviews.

feeds.title: Kaveesh Blog
feeds.description: This website is designed to help make reading books more enjoyable than ever before. Here, you'll find tips, lists, news, Books lovers will also find plenty of content about libraries, reading, and gift ideas.

feeds.title: Wanda Luthman's Children's Books
feeds.description: Wanda Luthman' is an author of Children's Books. A Blog dedicated to encouraging good character in children through quality literature.

feeds.title: Reading With Your Kids Blog
feeds.description: We are dedicated to encouraging parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles and anyone who is caring for a child, to spend more time reading together. Join us as we interview award-winning, best selling children's authors from around the World.

feeds.title: Literacy, families and learning
feeds.description: A blog about children's literacy, language, learning and teaching in families and schools.

feeds.title: Library Mice
feeds.description: I am based in the South West of England, I am a school librarian by profession, a mum of two, and I have a personal interest in children's literature, with particular interests in picture books and teen fiction.

feeds.title: Beagles and Books
feeds.description: A blog featuring reviews of children's literature.

feeds.title: 2 Kids and Tired Books
feeds.description: Holly is a mother of two. A northern California girl living in Idaho. A mom who loves to read and has a BA in English and a Certificate in Technical Writing and also does freelance editing and transcription at home part time.

feeds.title: Red Reading Hub Blog
feeds.description: Follow this blog to get reviews of children's books, books about children and education

feeds.title: Story Snug
feeds.description: Story Snug recommends books rather than review them so that our blog followers know that when a book is on Story Snug we have personally read it and enjoyed it. Story Snug's main critic is six years old, if she likes a book it goes on the blog, if not then it doesn't. The only exception to this is the books that are recommended on our author / illustrator guest posts.

feeds.title: Library Girl and Book Boy
feeds.description: Jo is a primary teacher in the specialist provision, reading consultant & book blogger. Through this blog, she aims to introduce children, their families, teachers, and book-lovers to books they may not have come across before but would enjoy reading or using in their school curriculums.

feeds.title: Get Kids into Books
feeds.description: Blogging about the children's books we love. Rachel Caddick is passionate about children's books and about children enjoying books & reading. By writing this blog, she hopes to share this passion and to get kids into books.

feeds.title: Orange Marmalade Books
feeds.description: At Orange Marmalade Books, Jill dedicates herself to promoting delightful children's literature. As a mother to four remarkable individuals engaged in work, travel, and study across diverse locations, her passion for books dates back to her early years in the 60s. Jill's enduring love for exceptional children's literature remains steadfast, inspiring her to share the joys of reading with others through her platform.

feeds.title: What to Read to Your Kids
feeds.description: Melissa LaSalle, known affectionately as The Book Mommy, resides in Alexandria, Virginia, with her husband and two children. With nearly three decades of expertise in children's literature, she's a beacon of inspiration for fostering literary cultures at home. Through What to Read to Your Kids, Melissa shares her passion for reading, offering unique recommendations across all ages. Her curated selections reflect her unwavering dedication to instilling the love of books in families far and wide.

feeds.title: Always in the Middle…
feeds.description: Always in the Middle is a blog about Middle-grade book reviews, giveaways, and writing tips from Greg Pattridge. Discover Middle-grade fiction and non-fiction books to make your kids smarter. Greg runs Always in the Middle and is a teacher, mentor, and writer.

feeds.title: Vivian Kirkfield
feeds.description: My blog has simple recipes, quick and easy crafts, picture book reviews and author interviews.

feeds.title: Write What Inspires You
feeds.description: Award-winning children's author, Donna McDine, shares her writing and marketing tips along with her journey in becoming a children's author. As well as promoting fellow children's authors.

feeds.title: Sarah Webb Blog
